newsitem.title: USA: Key to Oklahoma bombing truck found - prosecutors.
newsitem.headline: Key to Oklahoma bombing truck found - prosecutors.

text.p: Investigators found the key to the rented Ryder truck that prosecutors claim was used in the Oklahoma City bombing, lead prosecutor Joe Hartzler revealed in court Tuesday.

The disclosure that the key was found in an alley near the bombing site came while the prosecution's star witness, Michael Fortier, was on the stand in the trial of Timothy McVeigh, accused of the April 1995 bombing.

Hartzler asked Fortier only a few questions, including one intended to show that he could not have found out from media accounts that McVeigh planned to park the truck bomb in an alley next to the YMCA building, as Fortier had told authorities.

Hartzler then revealed that the key had been found in the alley. The government has produced more than 90 witnesses who have testified about McVeigh's anger at the government, his plans for the bombing and his use of a pre-paid telephone calling card to shop for components to make the bomb.
Fortier, 28, who has pleaded guilty to four felony counts in exchange for his testimony, was cross-examined on Monday and Tuesday by chief defense attorney Stephen Jones.

On Monday, Fortier offered damaging testimony that McVeigh plotted to blow up the Oklahoma City federal building to avenge the deaths of 80 cult members at Waco, Texas, in April 1993 and spark a "general uprising" against the government. McVeigh has pleaded not guilty to planning and executing the bombing, which killed 168 people.
